extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants, patent draftspersons, and patent examiners (preparing and reviewing patent drawings)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and examiner guidance from the MPEP governing the content, form, submission, correction, and handling of drawings (including color photographs/drawings) for U.S. utility, plant, and design patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to accept color drawings or color photographs
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition under 37 CFR 1.84(a)(2) to permit color drawings or color photographs must be accompanied by the appropriate fee (37 CFR 1.17(h)), three sets of color drawings or color photographs as appropriate, and, unless already present, an amendment to include specified language as the first paragraph of the brief description of the drawings section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the exact form paragraph notifying that the file contains color drawings and that copies will be provided by the Office upon request and payment. Color photographs will be accepted only if the conditions for accepting color drawings and black and white photographs are satisfied (see 37 CFR 1.84(b)(2)). Petition will normally be granted only when the USPTO determines color is the only practical medium to disclose the subject matter in a printed utility patent. Filing desired color drawings/photos with the original application is emphasized to avoid statutory defects (e.g., lack of enablement under 35 U.S.C. 112 or new matter under 35 U.S.C. 132). Do not use the form paragraph for black and white photographs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic drawing symbols and legends
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphic drawing symbols and other labeled representations may be used for conventional elements where appropriate, subject to approval by the Office (37 CFR 1.84(n)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitable legends may be used or required in proper cases; see the USPTO 'Guide for the Preparation of Patent Drawings'. ANSI publications (e.g., symbols for fluid power diagrams, logic functions, electrical diagrams) are generally acceptable as guides, but the Office will not approve a published collection of symbols as a group — use and clarity are decided case-by-case. Avoid overly specific symbols; label symbols with unclear meanings for clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of conventional symbols to indicate materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specified symbols to indicate various materials where the material is an important feature of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventional features/symbols are helpful for prior-art searches. When material composition is important to the invention, apply the conventional material hatchings/symbols (see MPEP figures/guides).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings must be readable and reproducible for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: OPAP will accept drawings if they are readable and reproducible for publication purposes; drawings are either acceptable or not acceptable (the Office no longer distinguishes formal vs informal drawings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should review drawings for disclosure of the claimed invention and for proper use of reference numerals. Objections to drawings in utility or plant applications will not be held in abeyance absent specific Office notification (37 CFR 1.85(a)). Corrections should be made promptly before allowance to avoid delays in issuance or reductions in term adjustment (37 CFR 1.704(c)(10)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings must show every claimed feature (complete illustration)
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing in a nonprovisional application must show every feature of the invention specified in the claims (37 CFR 1.83(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventional features whose detailed illustration is not essential may be illustrated as graphical symbols or labeled representations (e.g., labeled rectangular boxes). Tables and sequence listings are not permitted in the drawings (except for applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 371). If the invention is an improvement on an old machine, when possible show the improved portion disconnected from the old structure in one or more views and also show just enough of the old structure in another view to show the connection (37 CFR 1.83(b)). Any structural detail of sufficient importance to be described should be shown in the drawing (Ex parte Good).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner requirement for additional illustration
rubrics_metrics.description: When drawings do not comply with 37 CFR 1.83(a) or (b), the examiner shall require such additional illustration within a time period of not less than two months from the date of notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such correction periods are subject to the requirements of 37 CFR 1.81(d). Use appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 6.22.01, 6.22.04, 6.36) to require illustration. Provide clear identification of missing details in bracketed text of form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement/corrected drawings submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrected or replacement drawing sheets submitted after the filing date must comply with 37 CFR 1.121(d) and each sheet must be labeled in the top margin as either 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet' (37 CFR 1.84(c), 1.121(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amended replacement sheet should include all figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet, even if only one figure is being amended. Do not label a figure or figure number as 'amended'. If canceling a figure, remove it from the replacement sheet and renumber remaining figures; update the brief description of the several views accordingly. Additional replacement sheets may be necessary to show renumbering. Failure to timely submit replacements can result in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marked-up (annotated) copies required with corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to replacement sheets containing corrected figure(s), applicant is required to submit a marked-up copy of each replacement sheet including annotations indicating the changes made to the previous version (37 CFR 1.121(d)(1)/(d)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked-up copies must be clearly labeled 'Annotated Sheet' and must be presented in the amendment or remarks section explaining the changes. Failure to timely submit the corrected drawing and marked-up copy will result in abandonment of the application. Examiners should request annotated copies when using corresponding form paragraphs (e.g., may follow with form paragraph 6.27).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines and abandonment for untimely or missing drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a drawing is not timely received in reply to a notice from the Office or an examiner's letter requiring a drawing, the application becomes abandoned; Office notices set specific reply periods (e.g., two months or three months) and some are extendable under 37 CFR 1.136(a) while others are non-extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP will send a Notice to File Corrected Application Papers giving applicant a time period of 2 months from mailing to file acceptable drawings (extendable under 1.136(a)). If corrections are required at allowance, Office may set a three-month period from mailing of the notice of allowability to file corrected drawings to avoid abandonment; that three-month period is not extendable under 1.136(a) or (b). Use appropriate extension procedure where permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPAP processing and examiner handling of unacceptable drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: OPAP reviews drawings for compliance with certain requirements of 37 CFR 1.84 and will not release applications to Technology Centers until acceptable drawings are filed; the Office will not release drawings for purposes of correction (37 CFR 1.85(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If OPAP finds drawings unacceptable, it will notify applicant to file new acceptable drawings. If examiner believes drawings prevent reasonable examination, corrected drawings should be required immediately; if drawings permit reasonable examination but are defective under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, examination may begin with requirement for corrected drawings and a 112 rejection. If the drawing is admitted for examination but defects exist, the objection will not be held in abeyance and an amendment with corrected drawings is required to be fully responsive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners must ensure completeness and consistency of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should ensure the figures are correctly described in the brief description of the several views, reference characters are properly applied, no single reference character is used for two different parts or for a part and its modification, and there are no superfluous illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs (e.g., 6.22.03) to require correction when reference characters are used for multiple parts or other inconsistencies exist. When specific defects are found, identify them in the bracketed form paragraph text and require corrected sheets pursuant to 1.121(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference characters must appear consistently in drawings and specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings objected to for failing to include reference signs mentioned in the description (37 CFR 1.84(p)(5)) or for including reference characters not mentioned in the description require corrected drawing sheets or amendment to the specification to add/delete the reference characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In objecting, specify the reference characters not found and cite the page/line of their first occurrence in the specification. The Office may allow applicant to delete the reference characters from the description instead of adding them to the drawings. Use form paragraphs 6.22.06 and 6.22.07 where appropriate; objections will not be held in abeyance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not introduce new matter in replacement drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: It is applicant's responsibility to ensure that no new matter is added when submitting replacement drawings after allowance since replacement drawings will not normally be reviewed by an examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner notices new matter in replacement drawings, appropriate action to have the new matter deleted should be undertaken. Be cautious when submitting replacement drawings after allowance to avoid raising new matter issues under 35 U.S.C. 132.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications depiction rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifications may not be shown in broken lines on figures which show in solid lines another form of the invention (Ex parte Badger). All modifications described must be illustrated, or the text canceled, except for mere references to minor variations or well-known and conventional parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a figure shows modified forms of construction in the same view, require corrected drawing sheets in compliance with 1.121(d) (use form paragraph 6.22.05). Avoid mixing alternative embodiments in ambiguous ways on a single figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art figures normally unnecessary and should be labeled
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures showing the prior art are usually unnecessary and should be canceled; however, where needed to understand applicant's invention they may be retained if designated by a legend such as 'Prior Art'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a prior art figure is retained, designate it clearly (form paragraph 6.36.01). If prior art figures are not labeled, use form paragraph 6.36.01 or 6.36. Note that prior art depictions should be minimized unless essential to understanding the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling and content requirements for replacement sheets and headers
rubrics_metrics.description: Each replacement drawing sheet should include the application number and the art unit in the upper center margin (37 CFR 1.84(c)) and be labeled in the header as 'Replacement Sheet' to avoid obstructing portions of drawing figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the application number and art unit exactly as directed to avoid misdirected drawings. For image file wrapper (IFW) processing, maintain original photographs or color drawings in an artifact folder as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PTO-948 and form paragraphs to notify applicant of drawing objections
rubrics_metrics.description: If original drawings are not acceptable, examiners may use a 2-part form PTO-948 to indicate objections and require new corrected drawings; examiners are directed to advise applicants in the first Office action of reasons why drawings are not acceptable (see MPEP § 707.07(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs (e.g., ¶6.21, ¶6.22, ¶6.26, ¶6.27, ¶6.22.01, ¶6.22.04, ¶6.22.03, ¶6.22.05, ¶6.22.06, ¶6.22.07, ¶6.36.01) provide template wording identifying reasons for objection and required corrective action. Provide specific bracketed explanations (e.g., identify missing details, reference numbers, or conflicting numbering) and, where appropriate, require annotated replacement sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage and file wrapper handling of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawing prints must be kept on top of the papers on the right side of the file wrapper under any bibliographic data sheet if the application is maintained in paper; for IFW, original photographs or color drawings may be maintained in an artifact folder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If drawings cannot be located, applications may be sent to issue or to the Files Repository without the original drawing; for an application sent to issue with missing drawings see MPEP § 608.02(z). For abandoned applications sent to the Files Repository, note on the contents that drawings were missing. Upon initial processing, original drawings are placed in the center portion of the file wrapper under the specification (paper files).
